title: Wine Wimsey Review · Sun Nov 1
subtitle: 16 feed (14 images + 2 TOBIs at #5 and #12) and 4 stories for Sunday Nov 1 · ISO week 44 is even, Sunday = 2 TOBIs · CHARACTER: The Hot Mess · 0 inbox items (inbox had nothing new, all 20 posts written fresh) · Captions: 6 SHORT, 8 SEE MORE · EXPERIMENT: #4 (fake age quiz, new format) and #15 (nostalgia object) · Not the extra batch: this is the regular Nov 1 batch, separate from the Nov 1 extra · FLAGS: a separate Nov 1 EXTRA batch already exists for the same posting date, so if both are uploaded Nov 1 gets 30 feed posts and 8 stories; #10 sign shows a plain P icon (not words)

posts.quote: I got a free tote bag for donating blood once. Eleven years later it's holding my whole life.
posts.caption: The bag has outlasted two cars, one phone, and a long run of better-looking bags. It's the color of oatmeal now, and not by design.
posts.first: It holds a flashlight, a stapler, three pens, a library book that is overdue, and half a sandwich from Tuesday. I have not found the thing I actually need in it since 2019. The bag still seems very responsible about all of it.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun hugging an overstuffed oatmeal canvas tote bag in a cluttered hallway, a glass of red wine on the table behind her. Text in the speech bubble reads: I got a free tote bag for donating blood once. Eleven years later it's holding my whole life.

posts.quote: My mattress has a 100-night trial. I'm on night 14 and already negotiating with my lower back.
posts.caption: It arrived rolled up in a box the size of a refrigerator, and I stood in the hallway and watched it unroll like a small event. The instructions said to wait twenty-four hours for it to reach full shape. I waited, then lay on it for roughly nine minutes, thinking very carefully about my spine. My lower back has taken no position yet. It's gathering evidence. There's a form I'd fill out to send it back, and I printed it and put it on the nightstand next to the glass, where important documents go.
posts.first: On night nine I rolled over at 3 a.m. and woke up facing the wall, which has never once happened in this house. I took it as progress. My back sent a twinge in response, which I'm choosing to read as maybe.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun sitting on the edge of a new mattress with one hand on her lower back and a paper tag in the other, giving it a side-eye, a glass of red wine on the nightstand. Text in the speech bubble reads: My mattress has a 100-night trial. I'm on night 14 and already negotiating with my lower back.

posts.quote: The shelf came with one extra screw. I decided it's a spare. The shelf leans left and has its own opinion.
posts.caption: The instructions said forty-five minutes and showed a smiling cartoon man doing it alone. I'd like a word with him. Two hours in, I had every piece laid out on the rug like a crime scene, a drill battery at eleven percent, and a growing suspicion that step six was written by someone who hates me. The shelf is up now. It leans left by about an inch, which I've decided is character. I put the books on it quickly so it couldn't change its mind. So far it's holding, mostly out of spite.
posts.first: Behind the box I found a small plastic bag labeled Extra Hardware. I looked at it for a while and put it in the junk drawer, which is where all my extra hardware lives. It has a lot of company in there. Eventually one of them will turn out to matter.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun holding up a single screw and an allen key beside a crooked leaning bookshelf and scattered cardboard, a glass of red wine on the floor. Text in the speech bubble reads: The shelf came with one extra screw. I decided it's a spare. The shelf leans left and has its own opinion.

posts.quote: I took a quiz that told me my real age. It was a number I wouldn't say out loud, so I closed the tab and took a different quiz.
posts.caption: It asked about my sleep, my stairs, and whether I remember a rotary phone. The results page had a lot of confidence.
posts.first: The second quiz said I had the energy of a thirty-eight-year-old. It asked me about snacks and nothing else. I'm accepting that one and filing the first under rumor. Both wanted my email address, which was the only part I declined.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun on a sofa with an open laptop on her knees, mouth open in shock, lowering the screen with one hand and holding a glass of red wine in the other, a dog and a cat asleep nearby. Text in the speech bubble reads: I took a quiz that told me my real age. It was a number I wouldn't say out loud, so I closed the tab and took a different quiz.

posts.quote: Changed the smoke detector battery without help. I'm taking the rest of the afternoon off.
posts.first: The old one had been chirping at 3 a.m. for two weeks, always right when I was almost asleep. I stood on a chair, which I regret as a decision but not as an outcome. It worked on the first try. I haven't felt this capable since the garden hose.

posts.quote: I told the pharmacist I'd just wait. She looked at the line, then at the one chair, and said I might want to bring a snack.
posts.caption: There was one chair, and a man in it who appeared to be asleep. I stood by the blood pressure machine for a while, as if that were the plan.
posts.first: When my name got called I had forgotten why I was there for about four seconds. The pharmacist said to take my time, and I felt that deeply. I walked out with the right bag and a coupon for a flu shot I'd already had.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun sitting on the only chair in a pharmacy waiting area, chin on her hand, holding a granola bar, a long line of people ahead of her at the counter. Text in the speech bubble reads: I told the pharmacist I'd just wait. She looked at the line, then at the one chair, and said I might want to bring a snack.

posts.quote: I slept wrong and now my neck has opinions until Thursday.
posts.caption: I did nothing to cause this, and that's the part I keep telling people. Saturday night I was asleep. Sunday morning I couldn't look left. I've been turning my whole body like a ship in a canal to check on the dog, who has noticed and now stands slightly to my left on purpose. I called my sister and she said she once did the same thing by sneezing. We spent ten minutes comparing injuries from nothing at all, which is the one competitive sport I'm still good at. I'm on the couch tonight, and the pillow has been told to behave.
posts.first: I tried the heating pad and woke up warm and tilted the other way. So now I'm even, which is more than I've managed with most things. The dog thinks it's a game and keeps standing where I can't see him.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun in a bright kitchen, head tilted stiffly, one hand clamped on her neck and a coffee mug in the other, a sleepy dog watching from the corner. Text in the speech bubble reads: I slept wrong and now my neck has opinions until Thursday.

posts.quote: I paid for a gym membership in January. It has been the most reliable thing in my life, because it shows up every month without me.
posts.caption: The fob lives on my key ring between the house key and one I've never identified. It has been to more places with me than the gym ever has.
posts.first: Every month the charge shows up on my statement and I feel a small flicker of support, like having a friend who's doing great. I wave at the building when I drive past. It waves back by existing.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun at her front door holding a key ring with a small gym fob and a sheepish half-smile, a couch and a glass of red wine visible behind her. Text in the speech bubble reads: I paid for a gym membership in January. It has been the most reliable thing in my life, because it shows up every month without me.

posts.quote: I own seven chargers and not one of them reaches the outlet by the couch.
posts.caption: I'm not sure where the seven chargers came from. I only remember buying two. Last week I sat on the living room floor and untangled all of them, which took forty minutes and a small amount of language. Four fit nothing I own. One is for a camera I sold in 2014. The one I need fits perfectly and is, I measured, eleven inches too short to reach the outlet by the couch. I moved the couch once and gave up. Now I charge my phone in the kitchen and visit it every so often, like a patient.
posts.first: I bought a longer cord yesterday. It arrived today with a plug that doesn't fit the phone. I've added it to the drawer, which now holds more cords than I have things to plug in. The drawer is doing great.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun sitting on a living room floor with a tangle of charging cables in her lap, one cable stretched taut and falling short of a wall outlet, a glass of red wine on the side table. Text in the speech bubble reads: I own seven chargers and not one of them reaches the outlet by the couch.

posts.quote: I got a parking ticket for a spot I've used for twenty years. The sign changed. I did not.
posts.caption: Twenty years in that spot. The sign has a new set of hours and, I'm told, has had them since March. It's a lot to find out in one afternoon.
posts.first: The ticket was forty-five dollars. I stood on the curb long enough that a man walking by wondered if I was waiting for someone. I said the city, and he nodded like that was reasonable and kept going.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun on a city sidewalk beside a parking sign pole, one hand on her hip and a small orange ticket in the other, one eyebrow raised, a parked grey sedan behind her. Text in the speech bubble reads: I got a parking ticket for a spot I've used for twenty years. The sign changed. I did not.

posts.quote: My doctor's office sent a reminder, a reminder for the reminder, and then a call to say I was late.
posts.caption: The first reminder came Monday, the second on Tuesday, and a third arrived Wednesday morning to remind me about the other two. Then the front desk called at 9:40 for a 9:30 appointment. By then I was in the parking lot of the wrong building, holding a coffee and a folder with the right paperwork for a different year. Everyone was very nice about it, which was worse. The woman on the phone offered Friday, then read me the date, time, and address twice, slowly, like she was defusing something. I wrote it on my hand. It's Thursday and my hand is mostly ink and good intentions.
posts.first: On Friday I arrived twenty minutes early and sat in the waiting room with a magazine from 2021 about how to have a calm autumn. The nurse called my name and I stood up too fast, which is its own appointment.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun in a kitchen holding a buzzing phone at arm's length with three colorful notification icons floating above it, a glass of red wine in the other hand, mouth open in a gasp. Text in the speech bubble reads: My doctor's office sent a reminder, a reminder for the reminder, and then a call to say I was late.

posts.quote: Day three in the same sweatpants. The dryer has started to take it personally.
posts.first: Day three of the same gray sweatpants. They've been through a Friday, a Saturday, and one very serious trip to the mailbox. I'm respecting the silence from the dryer. Tomorrow I'll wear jeans, or the other sweatpants.

posts.quote: The plant tag said 'impossible to kill.' We're on week three and I'm taking it as a challenge.
posts.caption: The tag said it needs only light and occasional water. I've provided both with real conviction. It has dropped three leaves out of what looks like principle.
posts.first: I moved it to the window, then away from the window, then back. It's been in more locations than I have this month. A friend said talking to it helps, so I told it about my week. It listened about as well as everyone else does.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun squinting suspiciously at a droopy potted plant with fallen leaves on a sunny windowsill, a small plant tag in one hand and a glass of red wine in the other. Text in the speech bubble reads: The plant tag said 'impossible to kill.' We're on week three and I'm taking it as a challenge.

posts.quote: The streaming service checked whether I was still watching. I was, and I didn't love the tone.
posts.caption: It came up at 1:15 on a Sunday afternoon, which is when I do my best work. I had a blanket, a cat on my feet, and a show about people renovating a lighthouse in the rain. I'd planned to get up at the end of the episode and do something with my day. That was episode two. Now it's episode six and I know a great deal about load-bearing walls. The cat has moved twice, both times in disgust. I did get up once to refill a glass, and I'd call that a very structured afternoon overall.
posts.first: Dinner was cereal at 6 p.m. while the lighthouse got a new roof. I'm not proud of it, but I'm not hiding it either. The cat has said nothing, which tells me we're on the same page.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun on a couch under a blue blanket with a cat asleep on her feet, holding a remote and a glass of red wine and glaring flatly at a dark TV screen with a small play icon. Text in the speech bubble reads: The streaming service checked whether I was still watching. I was, and I didn't love the tone.

posts.quote: I found my old mixtape. I don't own anything to play it on, but I held it for a while like it might start.
posts.caption: The label said Songs for Driving, in handwriting I used to have. I found it in a shoebox with a dead battery, a Polaroid of a dog we had in the nineties, and a ticket stub from a concert I mostly attended for the parking. Side A was clearly made with great care, and side B was clearly made at 2 a.m. I sat on the bedroom floor and read the track listing like a letter. I don't know what happened to the tape deck. I think about its absence more than I expected, and the tape is going on the shelf.
posts.first: My sister swears the dog in the Polaroid is the one from the cabin trip. It's definitely a different dog. I let her have it. We've agreed to disagree, and I'm keeping the picture.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun sitting on a bedroom floor beside an open shoebox of cassette tapes, holding one cassette to her ear with her eyes closed and a soft smile, a glass of red wine and a sleeping cat nearby. Text in the speech bubble reads: I found my old mixtape. I don't own anything to play it on, but I held it for a while like it might start.

posts.quote: Restaurants have started printing the menus smaller. I'm not saying it's a conspiracy. I'm saying I held mine at arm's length until the waiter offered to read it to me.
posts.caption: The waiter was kind enough to wait until the third attempt. I hold the menu out at full arm's length, then pull it close, then tilt it toward the candle like I'm reading a treasure map. Nobody at my table said a word. My friend Joanne just slid her phone across with the flashlight on, the way you'd hand someone a tissue. I'm grateful and I'm not discussing it. We ordered the soup because I could read the word soup. It was good soup, and I'd tell you what else was on the menu, but I'll never know.
posts.first: I bought drugstore readers the next morning, three pairs, in case I lose two. One lives in the car, one by the bed, one in my purse. They're the same pair of readers in different places. I've never felt more organized.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun at a candlelit restaurant table holding an open menu at full arm's length with a hard squint, a glass of red wine on the table. Text in the speech bubble reads: Restaurants have started printing the menus smaller. I'm not saying it's a conspiracy. I'm saying I held mine at arm's length until the waiter offered to read it to me.
